stories.title: Von der Leyen pushing EU toward war with Russia — Finnish politician
stories.summary: Armando Mema said the European Commission president tends to baselessly accuse Russia of violating the airspace of European countries
article_sentences: STOCKHOLM, August 21.

A member of Finland’s national-conservative Freedom Alliance party, Armando Mema, accused European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen of hypocrisy for urging EU countries to rearm over an alleged threat from Russia while also saying that preserving peace is the bloc’s main mission.
"Ursula von der Leyen says that the mission of the EU is to preserve Peace.
<...> No matter how beautifully Ursula might speak, the 800-billion-euro re-armament is the biggest threat to Peace.
Russia will see it as a direct threat to its security.
It appears clear that the EC President is affected by hallucinations and mental instability, Russia does not have any intention to attack Europe," the Finnish politician wrote on his X page.
He stressed that von der Leyen tends to baselessly accuse Russia of violating the airspace of European countries.
At the same time, she deliberately ignores the Nord Stream explosions, which, according to a preliminary investigation by Germany’s Federal Prosecutor General’s Office, involved Ukrainian nationals.
"Ursula is doing nothing for Peace, is in fact doing everything in the opposite direction for War," Mema added.

stories.title: Moroccan families travel to Ceuta border in search of missing loved ones
stories.summary: CEUTA, Spain – Moroccan families are searching for loved ones who left last month for the Spanish enclave of Ceuta during a large wave of migration. Many of them are camping outside the Tarajal border post on the Moroccan side in hopes of obtaining information. Spain has set up a special office for missing persons.

stories.title: Djibouti Football Federation accused of misusing funds from FIFA
stories.summary: The tiny Horn of Africa nation of Djibouti is embroiled in a football corruption row after a government audit accused its federation, largely funded by FIFA, of favouritism and inadequate competitive bidding. The recent success of Cape Verde – which reached the knockout stage of the 2026 FIFA World Cup – has shown that small African nations can succeed with the right organisation. Djibouti footballers are furious, however, at their federation over allegations it has misused money from world football governing body FIFA, which provides the vast majority of its funding. Funds provided by Saudi Arabia for a new headquarters for the Djibouti Football Federation are also said to have been misused. One local club manager, speaking on condition of anonymity, told the AFP news agency that his team would boycott this year’s league unless there was a change in leadership. “The (Djibouti federation’s) resources are not used for the development of football,” he alleged. “When I see what Cape Verde is capable of achieving… I tell myself there is a structural problem within our federation,” he added. The allegations stem from a 2024 government inspector’s report, recently obtained by AFP, that accuses the federation of “favouritism” in awarding the contract for the headquarters and overpricing for many elements of the contract. FIFA, which along with the Confederation of African Football (CAF) provides more than $1m a year to Djibouti’s federation, did not respond to queries from AFP. A member of Djibouti’s federation, Mohamed Elmi Farah, resigned from its executive committee on August 12 August, expressing “concerns regarding the management and use of the federation’s resources”. Souleiman Hassan Waberi, the longtime head of the Djibouti Football Federation, told AFP it had been cleared of all wrongdoing by FIFA. “FIFA has officially confirmed to us that, to date, its monitoring mechanisms have revealed no indication of wrongdoing regarding the funds it disbursed,” said Waberi, who also serves on the FIFA Council as a representative of CAF.

stories.title: E1 Israeli settlement poses ‘existential threat’ to two-state solution, UN chief warns
stories.summary: The United Nations on Wednesday said UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres was alarmed by reports of illegal Israeli settlement outposts in the West Bank, warning that development in the E1 area threatened a two-state solution. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said the E1 settlement would sever the connection between the northern and southern West Bank and have severe consequences for the territory’s integrity.

stories.title: What a record-breaking El Nino could mean for the world
stories.summary: This year's El Nino is on track to be the strongest on record, threatening to unleash extreme weather across the globe and make 2027 the hottest recorded year by far. It is expected to be the most "intense" El Nino in more than a century, the head of long-range forecasting at the UK's Met Office warned on Friday. Stacked on top of long-term human-caused climate change, the temporary jolt will offer a glimpse of the heat the world can expect by the late 2030s, experts say.
